<!-- factory-audit-2026-10-16:deploy-retry -->

Parent: #17. Related intake defect: #1. Audit report: [source audit and delivery plan](https://github.com/bin0110001/cezar-factory/blob/7708c1e/docs/factory-audit-2026-10-16.md). Documentation PR: #24.

## Objective and evidence

scripts/deploy/factory-autodeploy.sh advances the checkout before checking container parity and reconciling automations. A failure there leaves HEAD at stable. The next timer run sees changed=0 and exits before either failed operation, so recovery requires --force or another commit. The current parity check compares VERSION only, which cannot distinguish same-version source drift.

Source: local 767ac01, cross-checked against dev addbd38. This is a source finding, not proof of a live incident.

## Proposed implementation

Track last successfully reconciled SHA separately from checkout HEAD, retry incomplete parity/synchronization on unchanged SHA, and record success only after every configured target and runtime check passes. Include commit/content identity in runtime parity. Keep the existing lock and dirty/divergent refusal semantics.

## Dependencies

#21

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Inject a one-time reconciliation failure after checkout advancement; the next ordinary timer invocation retries and succeeds without --force.
- [ ] Container parity failure is retried until fixed and cannot write a successful receipt.
- [ ] A fully successful unchanged SHA follows an explicitly documented health/drift reconciliation policy.
- [ ] Dirty/divergent checkout and missing target config fail without overwriting state.
- [ ] Parity detects stale same-VERSION runtime content.

## Validation

Use a temporary Git remote and stub podman/sync commands to cover failure then retry, process interruption, concurrent lock, same-version drift, dirty and divergent trees. Validate shell syntax and run repository checks.

## Scope and gates

No host checkout edits, reset/clean/stash operations, or unapproved service rollout. Human plan approval is required.

Human plan approval is required before implementation. This proposed plan is not that approval.

Required reading: AGENTS.md, policies/definition-of-ready.md, policies/risk.yaml, the files cited above, docs/shared-factory.md and the audit report. Factory-managed changes must be committed, pushed, independently reviewed through a dev PR, released to every explicitly configured target, and verified before closure.

<!-- factory-audit-2026-10-16:validation -->

Parent: #17. Related intake defect: #1. Audit report: [source audit and delivery plan](https://github.com/bin0110001/cezar-factory/blob/7708c1e/docs/factory-audit-2026-10-16.md). Documentation PR: #24.

## Objective and evidence

scripts/factory/test-full.ps1 and test-changed.ps1 derive artifacts from $PSScriptRoot, so all shared-mount runs write scripts/artifacts/*-results.json. test-full recursively executes source files instead of project test runners, repeats tests/Tests on case-insensitive filesystems, and reports passed/exit 0 for zero tests. Both outer catches can write status=failed without incrementing the counter controlling exit.

Source: local 767ac01, cross-checked against dev addbd38. This is a source finding, not proof of a live incident.

## Proposed implementation

Use the existing validation.changed/full/verify entries in factory.config.yaml and project-owned scripts/factory adapters, rather than introducing a second configuration schema. The workflow currently calls shared wrappers directly. Resolve configured commands from the current project/worktree, invoke child processes with bounded output, and put all results under worktree-local .factory/artifacts/<run-or-step>. Preserve an explicit no-tests/skipped outcome distinct from passed. Provide migration guidance for installed and shared projects.

## Dependencies

None; can be planned independently.

Required by: #20

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An isolated empty project cannot be reported as a passing full suite; unsupported projects return an actionable skipped/error policy outcome.
- [ ] Representative PowerShell, .NET, JS/TS and Godot projects invoke their configured runner once, including on Windows.
- [ ] Any runner/setup exception or nonzero exit produces a nonzero wrapper exit and matching failure artifact.
- [ ] Two concurrent worktrees never overwrite each other's artifacts or write into the shared runtime.

## Validation

Add fixture-driven subprocess tests for configured runners, empty projects, setup exceptions, nonzero exits, missing commands, spaces in paths and concurrent artifact isolation. Run the Factory suite on Windows and Linux.

## Scope and gates

Do not redesign GitHub merge routing or add automatic discovery of arbitrary project commands.

Plan before execution; independent review and validated release are required.

<!-- factory-audit-2026-10-16:merge-gates -->

Parent: #17. Related intake defect: #1. Audit report: [source audit and delivery plan](https://github.com/bin0110001/cezar-factory/blob/7708c1e/docs/factory-audit-2026-10-16.md). Documentation PR: #24.

## Objective and evidence

scripts/validate-result.ps1 accepts status=success with testResult=failed, acceptanceCriteriaStatus=Not met and knownConcerns=Unresolved blocker (reproduced, exit 0). scripts/route-state.ps1 review-result sends the supplied PR URL directly to gh pr merge --auto without reading the PR base, current head, required checks or independent review. Repository auto-merge is currently disabled; dev protection returns HTTP 404.

Source: local 767ac01, cross-checked against dev addbd38. This is a source finding, not proof of a live incident.

## Proposed implementation

Define authoritative validation and review receipts bound to issue, repository, PR and head SHA. Reject contradictory success data, verify the current PR targets dev, verify required validation and independent review at that SHA, enforce high-risk plan approval, and fail closed before any merge request. Report queued auto-merge separately from observed merge completion. Document required GitHub settings without enabling them in this implementation task.

## Dependencies

#19

Required by: #21

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A success result with failed/not-run tests or unmet criteria fails validation; meaningful failure results remain representable.
- [ ] Wrong-repository/base PRs, changed heads, failed/pending required checks, unresolved findings and missing independent review cannot request merge.
- [ ] High-risk work without human plan approval cannot request merge.
- [ ] Disabled auto-merge or missing configured review/check gates produces a concrete blocker and never a false success.
- [ ] Completion receipts distinguish an auto-merge request from an observed merge.

## Validation

Use fake GitHub subprocess/API fixtures to assert no merge command occurs for each rejected case; test one valid reviewed dev PR and a head-change race. Run the full Factory suite.

## Scope and gates

No branch protection changes, no bypassing checks or reviews, and no production rollout until a human approves this high-risk plan.

Human plan approval is required before implementation. This proposed plan is not that approval.

<!-- factory-audit-2026-10-16:release -->

Parent: #17. Related intake defect: #1. Audit report: [source audit and delivery plan](https://github.com/bin0110001/cezar-factory/blob/7708c1e/docs/factory-audit-2026-10-16.md). Documentation PR: #24.

## Objective and evidence

skills/factory-release/SKILL.md shared procedure omits merge-to-dev and contains a broken scripts/release path. skills/factory-finish-release/SKILL.md places promotion/synchronization before its reviewed PR step. scripts/release/promote-stable.ps1 promotes arbitrary clean HEAD and exposes a public -TestScript replacement despite claiming no test bypass; tests/run-tests.ps1 uses that hook. It does not verify HEAD belongs to reviewed merged dev history.

Source: local 767ac01, cross-checked against dev addbd38. This is a source finding, not proof of a live incident.

## Proposed implementation

Define one lifecycle: validate source -> reviewed dev PR -> observed merge -> resolve exact merged SHA -> full mandatory suite on that immutable tree -> stable promotion -> target synchronization -> runtime parity receipts. Keep test seams outside the production CLI, distinguish initial stable creation from fetch failures, and make shared/legacy target behavior explicit. Put operational scripts in workflow command steps and keep skills as artifact/gate guidance.

## Dependencies

#20

Required by: #18

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unmerged feature commits and an unreviewed/mismatched SHA cannot advance stable.
- [ ] The production entry point cannot replace/skip the mandatory full suite.
- [ ] Authentication/network failures fetching stable fail closed rather than being treated as a missing ref.
- [ ] Release and finish-release skills agree with AGENTS.md and docs/shared-factory.md, including command ownership.
- [ ] Each explicit target gets a receipt for the same reviewed source SHA; absent registry or parity mismatch stops safely.

## Validation

Test with temporary bare remotes: unmerged HEAD, failed suite, fetch error, absent stable, divergent stable, reviewed merged SHA, missing targets and parity mismatch. No external target writes in tests.

## Scope and gates

Do not alter host files by hand, invent targets, or implement infrastructure deployment beyond the supported flow. Human plan approval is required.

Human plan approval is required before implementation. This proposed plan is not that approval.

<!-- factory-audit-2026-10-16:collector -->

Parent: #17. Related intake defect: #1. Audit report: [source audit and delivery plan](https://github.com/bin0110001/cezar-factory/blob/7708c1e/docs/factory-audit-2026-10-16.md). Documentation PR: #24.

## Objective and evidence

scripts/audit-factory-failures.ps1 creates project and Factory issues although factory-failure-audit skill promises at most one. $evidenceText is assigned only when creating a new project issue; a deduplicated project issue can leave the Factory issue without evidence. Existing issue #1 has blank affected-project/recovery fields and no run evidence in its body; historical comments do contain two failed run IDs, affected project issue #371 and validation errors (https://github.com/bin0110001/cezar-factory/issues/1#issuecomment-6020442037). gh lookup failures are treated as no matches without checking LASTEXITCODE. /runs responses and handoff text are read before applying any bound; the limited status does not reflect all limitations.

Source: local 767ac01, cross-checked against dev addbd38. This is a source finding, not proof of a live incident.

## Proposed implementation

Build a compact, redacted evidence object before any write; use explicit registry/API project identity rather than guessing from a folder name; bound source reads/pagination, time window and output size. Decide and document whether one canonical Factory issue or a reciprocal pair is the contract, and use stable fingerprints plus qualified URLs. Fail closed on lookup/auth failures and preserve available evidence on partial writes. Separate recovery side effects from read-only collection.

## Dependencies

None; can be planned independently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New-project, existing-project and same-repository cases all preserve run/step/command evidence with full cross-repository links.
- [ ] A failed lookup creates no speculative duplicate; repeated audit runs deduplicate by stable fingerprint.
- [ ] Large handoffs/API histories obey declared read/output bounds and report truncation/time-window limitations.
- [ ] Partial cross-repository publication has an actionable receipt and can retry idempotently.
- [ ] The skill, workflow switches and collector agree on read/write and issue-count behavior; existing #1 is linked for triage without inventing evidence.

## Validation

Add fake-gh and fake-Cezar fixtures covering authentication failure, exact dedupe, existing project issue/new Factory issue, same repository, oversized evidence, missing runs and partial publication. Run the full suite.

## Scope and gates

Do not close or claim to fix existing intake issue #1, broaden filesystem discovery, or restart production workflows during tests.

Plan before execution; independent review and validated release are required.

Required reading: AGENTS.md, policies/definition-of-ready.md, policies/risk.yaml, the files cited above, docs/shared-factory.md and the audit report. Factory-managed changes must be committed, pushed, independently reviewed through a dev PR, released to every explicitly configured target, and verified before closure.

<!-- factory-audit-2026-10-16:contracts -->

Parent: #17. Related intake defect: #1. Audit report: [source audit and delivery plan](https://github.com/bin0110001/cezar-factory/blob/7708c1e/docs/factory-audit-2026-10-16.md). Documentation PR: #24.

## Objective and evidence

tests/run-tests.ps1 checks workflow shape with line regexes, skill existence/headings, and command-ownership phrases; it does not validate complete command contracts. plan/investigate startup RequiredScripts omit downstream validators/routers; intake omits downstream scripts. factory-fix JSON omits required issue and documentationUpdated; factory-review JSON omits required issue. factory-plan still instructs posting a comment although workflow routing owns it. factory-implement command discipline also says to invoke Factory scripts, contradicting its later prohibition and AGENTS.md. docs/workflow-map.md describes a superseded risk-based human merge path.

Source: local 767ac01, cross-checked against dev addbd38. This is a source finding, not proof of a live incident.

## Proposed implementation

Parse workflows with the same contract as the bundled Cezar runtime, validate skill references/retry targets/parameters and startup dependency coverage, and check copyable JSON examples against schemas. Separate schema-valid concrete examples from descriptive alternatives. Align skill responsibilities with workflow-owned routing and prepared artifacts; add negative mutations proving the checker catches drift. Cover all workflows, including scheduled and upgrade workflows.

## Dependencies

None; can be planned independently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Missing command script, unknown parameter, missing skill, invalid retry edge and incomplete startup dependency manifest fail checks with file/step diagnostics.
- [ ] Concrete skill examples validate against their result schemas; required issue/documentation fields are present.
- [ ] Skills cannot instruct duplicate issue discovery, routing/comments, or execution of workflow-owned scripts.
- [ ] A negative fixture for each contract class fails for the intended reason on Windows/Linux.
- [ ] Preserve the existing in-progress maintenance/backlog edits; reconcile rather than overwrite them.

## Validation

Run schema/contract checks against the real workflow inventory and deliberately mutated fixtures, followed by the full suite. Avoid relying only on source-string presence assertions.

## Scope and gates

Do not replace Cezar's engine, change model routing, or fold unrelated skill rewrites into this PR.

Plan before execution; independent review and validated release are required.
